# The True Size Map

> An interactive map that shows the real relative size of countries, continents and cities. Drag any
> place across a Mercator map and it resizes as it moves; flip the whole map to Equal Earth, the
> equal-area projection the UN General Assembly endorsed on 4 September 2026 by 164 votes to 1.

Site: https://truesizemap.ryandrilowell.com/
Source: https://github.com/ryandril/truesizemap (MIT)
Author: Ryandri Lowell — https://ryandrilowell.com

## What the UN actually decided

On 4 September 2026 the UN General Assembly adopted the "Correct the Map" resolution, introduced by
African Union member states and the Bahamas, by 164 votes to 1 with 6 abstentions. The United States
voted against. The resolution is **not binding** and does **not ban** the Mercator projection: it
encourages governments, schools, international organisations and technology companies to prefer
equal-area projections such as Equal Earth wherever relative size matters, while explicitly leaving
Mercator in place for maritime and aerial navigation, for which it remains suited.

## Why Mercator distorts size

Mercator (Gerardus Mercator, 1569) is conformal: it preserves angles, which is what makes it useful
for navigation, but area is inflated with distance from the equator, roughly in proportion to the
secant of the latitude. Greenland sits near the pole and is drawn many times too large; equatorial
Africa is drawn close to true. Equal Earth (Bojan Savric, Tom Patterson and Bernhard Jenny, 2018) is
equal-area: every country occupies its correct share of the map, at the cost of some shape distortion.

## Real figures, as computed by this site

Areas are integrated from the drawn boundaries on a sphere of radius 6371.0088 km, so they differ by a
fraction of a percent from published figures but always match what the map shows.

- Africa: 30.0 million km2. Greenland: 2.15 million km2. Africa is about 13.9 times Greenland.
- Africa is nearly as large as the United States, China, India and Europe combined (31.8 million km2).
- The United States (9.44 million km2) would cover roughly 31% of Africa.
- Africa is about 1.8 times the size of Russia (16.9 million km2), the largest country on Earth.
- Alaska (1.49 million km2) is about three quarters the size of Mexico (1.96 million km2).
- Greenland (2.15 million km2) is slightly smaller than the Democratic Republic of the Congo (2.33 million km2).

## Data sources

- Countries and continents: Natural Earth 1:50m admin-0 map units, public domain.
- Cities: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries (ODbL, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors), matched by
  Wikidata ID and clipped to the coastline, because many official city boundaries include open water.
  Only 504 major cities ship, because a large share of official boundaries describe a province or a
  historic core rather than the city, and a wrong number is worse than a missing one.
